title: Switzerland enterprise launch: messaging brief and sales enablement
body:
Purpose:
This brief is the go-to-market messaging and seller enablement anchor for Redwood Inference’s Switzerland enterprise launch (private deployments and dedicated capacity focus). It captures positioning, target segments, competitive differentiators, launch assets, and recommended field scripts for the first 90 days.

Launch objectives:
- Secure 6 pilot conversations with Swiss financial or healthcare enterprises within 90 days.
- Close 2 paid pilots (Dedicated or Private) by month 4.
- Validate data residency and KMS integrations with 1 major bank.

Primary audiences:
- Platform/AI engineering teams at regulated enterprises (banking, insurance, healthcare).
- Security/compliance decision-makers assessing data residency, key management, and auditability.
- Product managers evaluating latency and operational predictability for user-facing LLM features.

Core positioning statement (elevator pitch):
"Redwood Inference provides predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — giving Swiss enterprises the performance and data controls they need to put privacy-sensitive AI into production."

Why Switzerland matters (concise rationale):
- High density of regulated financial and healthcare institutions with strict data sovereignty needs.
- Large enterprise buyers prioritize SLAs, vendor transparency, and integration with Swiss/European KMS providers.
- Market willingness to pay for private deployments and compliance add-ons.

Key value props (top-line messaging to use in sales decks):
1) Data residency & control: Private deployments with customer-managed VPCs, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs designed for Swiss regulatory frameworks.
2) Predictable economics: Dedicated capacity options and cost-aware controls (batching, caching) reduce token spend while guaranteeing throughput.
3) Production-grade reliability: SLA-backed latency & availability, automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants, and a mature rollout engine for canary/A-B releases.
4) Developer ergonomics: Same Redwood API across hosted/dedicated/private—minimal rework when moving to private infra.

Supporting technical differentiators (talking points for engineers):
- GPU-optimized serving runtime with KV cache and sequence-length aware batching to preserve low tail latency.
- Kernel selection and quantization recommendations per workload to reduce unit cost without regressing quality.
- Smart request routing: policy-based routing (latency, cost, region) with automated fallback to ensure uptime during capacity spikes.

Competitive snapshot (notes for rebuttals):
- Major cloud AI endpoints: Good for quick prototyping but often lack private-deploy packaging and enterprise SLAs tailored to Swiss compliance teams. Emphasize Redwood’s private delivery and KMS integrations.
- LLM API vendors (pure-play APIs): May offer similar latency but often don’t provide dedicated pools or transparent per-token cost breakdowns for internal chargebacks.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: Present stronger data control but require customers to build orchestration, rollout tooling, and cost-optimization expertise that Redwood provides out-of-the-box.

Pricing guidance (sales-facing):
- Offer a two-stage commercial path: 6–12 week paid pilot (flat fee + metered usage) -> enterprise contract for Dedicated or Private deployment.
- For regulated buyers, quote a Private deployment with fixed monthly platform fee + support and optional on-prem deployment premium.

Field enablement snippets (short scripts):
- Initial outreach email subject: "Bring production-grade LLMs behind your VPC — Swiss data residency & SLAs"
- Opening line for discovery call: "We help teams run LLMs with predictable latency and enterprise controls (KMS, audit logs, private control plane). What are your top constraints: data residency, latency, or cost?"
- Technical discovery probe: "Do you need HSM/KMS integration for encryption at rest? What are your SLAs for inference latency and availability today?"

Launch timeline (high level):
- Week 0–2: Enable presales (sales training, technical playbook, demo infra).
- Week 3–6: Run targeted outbound to Swiss financial and healthcare accounts; 2 technical webinars (compliance-focused).
- Week 7–12: Start pilots, collect security questionnaires, iterate on deployment templates.
- Month 3–4: Close first commercial pilots and gather case material for localized marketing.

Assets required (checklist):
- Compliance one-pager (Swiss data residency checklist) — ready by W2.
- Sales deck (enterprise + technical appendix) — ready by W1.
- Demo scripts + terraform templates for Private deploy sandbox — ready by W2.
- Webinars: "Secure LLMs for Swiss Enterprises" (slides + replay) — W4.
- Customer FAQ and security questionnaire answers for presales.

Risk & mitigation notes:
- Risk: Long procurement cycles for regulated buyers. Mitigation: Start with short paid pilots and provide ready-to-sign security attachments (SaaS Data Processing Addendum, KMS patterns).
- Risk: Skepticism about performance of private/on-prem models. Mitigation: Publish latency benchmarks for typical sequences and offer short performance proof-of-concept during pilot.

Sample announcement copy (internal-simplified):
Subject: Switzerland enterprise launch — private deployment offering
Body: We’re formally launching Redwood Private and Dedicated sales offers into Switzerland, focusing on banks and healthcare. Key wins: data residency, enterprise SLAs, KMS integrations. Sales: engage with compliance early and offer a structured 6–12 week pilot to accelerate procurement.

Customer objection handling (short):
- "We can self-host and avoid vendor lock-in." -> "Self-hosting avoids vendor lock, but costs and time to production are often higher. Redwood bundles the runtime, rollout tooling, and ongoing optimizations so you can focus on product features instead of operational overhead."
- "How do you handle keys and auditability?" -> "We integrate with customer KMS/HSM, provide full audit logs, and document retention/rotation practices in the security appendix. We can run a technical session with your security team within 2 weeks of interest."

Post-launch measurement (success metrics):
- Number of pilots started and converted to paid by month 4.
- Average time from first contact to pilot kickoff.
- Sales velocity: cycle time for regulated customers compared to prior regions.
- Customer-reported latency and SLO adherence during pilot.

Next steps (owners):
- Sales enablement deck (Owner: Mateo Alvarez) — due 2025-10-02.
- Compliance one-pager & security FAQ (Owner: Nina Weber) — due 2025-09-25.
- Demo infra + terraform template (Owner: Owen Baker) — due 2025-09-29.

Open questions for leadership:
- Approve pilot commercial template (flat fee + metered usage) for Swiss regulated customers?
- Signoff on localized marketing spend for Q4?
